7.0.0.en: The greatest testimony to Noah is what God said of him here, that he was righteous, indeed the only one in his generation who believed in God and feared Him, so He commanded him to prepare to enter the ark, he, his wife, his three sons and their wives, to save them from destruction with the wicked.

7.0.1.en: Are you righteous in the eyes of God, that is, do you believe in Him and live with Him, and if you sin, hasten to repentance, confession and Holy Communion?

7.0.2.en: Do not be much preoccupied with people's praise, for it will not bring you into the Kingdom, but always examine your heart to be pure before God at all times.

7.1.0.en: In the previous chapter God commanded Noah to take into the ark a male and a female of all animals and birds (ch. 6:19, 20), in order to preserve all animals and birds for reproduction so that they would not perish. Here he mentions more details, commanding him to take seven pairs of the clean animals and birds and one pair of the unclean animals. This means that clean and unclean animals were known before the Law of Moses, and probably God had made them known to Adam, while the Law of Moses confirmed them and wrote them down. He took seven pairs of the clean animals and likewise of the birds so that he could offer sacrifices from them to God, for the clean animals alone are permitted for offering sacrifices, and also to eat of them, as God would permit him after he came out of the ark. He takes seven pairs of the birds because by their soaring in the air they signify loftiness and looking to heavenly things. As for the unclean animals and the birds of prey, of which man does not eat, God was content to take one pair of each, for His wisdom in preserving the balance of creation.

7.2.0.en: Every living substance: every living thing, whether man or animal.

7.2.1.en: God specified the period remaining until the beginning of the Flood, which was seven days, in which Noah would prepare himself and bring in the animals and all his needs and theirs, and God also specified the falling of the rain that would make the Flood as forty days. The number seven signifies the work of the Holy Spirit in preparing man to be saved from the evil of the world and for salvation in Christ, and it also signifies His work in the Church throughout the seven days of the week, which point to man's age and his life on earth. As for the number (40), it signifies the children of God who work by His Ten Commandments in the four corners of the world, for all the believers receive salvation in the ark, that is, in the Church, throughout their life on earth, and are saved from destruction with the wicked.

7.3.0.en: Noah was obedient to God with all exactness in all that He commanded him.

7.4.0.en: Noah was 480 years old when God commanded him to build the ark, and he continued 120 years building it, and thus preaching repentance to the whole world, but unfortunately no one believed. At the end of this period he was 600 years old, and he began to bring in the animals of their kinds and also the plants he would need as food for himself and the animals, and this procession moved quietly toward the ark for seven days, amid the mockery of the wicked and Noah's grief over their destruction and his last attempts to call them to repentance, until he had brought in all the animals and also his household.

7.4.1.en: What happened in the days of Noah happens today before your eyes when the Church calls you to repent and to enter into her so that you may find your salvation. If you make light of her words and persist in sin, God and all His saints look upon you with sorrow at your insistence on destroying your soul, so repent and cling to the Church and do not waste the rest of your life.

8.0.0.en: Remembered: this does not mean that God had forgotten Noah, but it shows His love and concern for him at this time.

8.0.1.en: A wind: wind and spirit in the original Hebrew are one word, so what is meant here is a wind and at the same time it is the power of the Holy Spirit of God that moved this air strongly so that the waters would abate. Assuaged: that is, the waters became calm because the falling of the rains and the bursting forth of the springs stopped, so they began to abate. Throughout the following hundred and fifty days the scene was terrifying, to declare the fear of God that destroyed the wicked and kept Noah and those with him righteous, far from sin. Then God showed His love for Noah and those with him by beginning the abating of the waters, so that the Flood, that is, God's wrath at the evil of mankind, would end. So He sent a strong wind to help evaporate the waters, either because of the heat of these winds or because these winds made cracks in the earth that helped the water seep into them. Thus the waters became calm and began to abate.

8.0.2.en: The Flood is a type of Baptism, in which the old man dies, that is, the nature inclined to evil, and the new man is born, that is, the nature inclined to good, just as the wicked died in the Flood and Noah was saved in the ark, which is a type of the Church of the New Testament, in which is the sacrament of Baptism. The wind that blew is a type of the Holy Spirit working in the sacrament of Baptism to give new life to everyone who is immersed in it.

8.1.0.en: After 150 days God stopped the falling of the rain and the coming out of water from the springs of the earth, so the waters became calm and began to evaporate into the air with the help of the wind and to seep into the earth, so they decreased and abated gradually.

8.2.0.en: After 37 days from the beginning of the abating of the waters, the top of a high mountain appeared, the mountain of "Ararat", that is, on the seventeenth day of the seventh month, because the lunar month is 30 days.

8.2.1.en: Some commentators say that this Mount Ararat is the one in Armenia.

8.3.0.en: The waters continued to abate gradually, and in the tenth month the tops of other mountains, lower than Mount Ararat, began to appear.

8.3.1.en: Would that the tribulations passing through the world do not disturb you but establish the fear of God in your heart, for He is your tender God who keeps you from all evil, but His wrath is fierce against the one who rejects the pure life, so this urges you to reject the evil that causes these problems, and be confident that God turns everything to your good and keeps you pure in His hands.

8.4.0.en: Forty days after the appearance of the mountain tops that appeared at the beginning of the tenth month, that is, on the eleventh day of the eleventh month of the six hundredth year of Noah's age, he wanted to find out how dry the earth was after the rains had stopped for five months and the waters had gradually abated, in addition to the ark's having rested on Mount Ararat for nearly four months. So he opened one of the windows of the ark and sent out a raven to fly and find out how dry the earth was, and he noticed the raven's going to and fro, that is, its going down to the earth and returning to the ark several times, since it found the remains of some stinking carcasses and ate of them, then returned to rest on top of the ark and went again to eat of these carcasses and returned several times.

8.4.1.en: The raven spiritually signifies the souls that are in the Church but love the evil world and its stinking desires and waver between life with God and life in sin.

8.5.0.en: Noah did not learn from the raven whether the earth had dried completely or not, so he sent out a gentle bird, the dove, which flew and wandered about and found no place to settle because of the presence of water, even if a little, on the earth, so it returned to Noah, who took it from the window and brought it inside the ark.

8.5.1.en: The dove signifies the pure soul that lives in the Church and finds no rest in the world defiled by sin.

8.6.0.en: Noah waited seven days for the remaining water on the earth to dry, and sent out the dove a second time. It flew all day, and in the evening it returned to him with an olive leaf in its mouth. This means that it found some shrubs or plants that had begun to appear in the slightly higher places, so it was able to settle on these shrubs all day and even eat of them, and it returned in the evening with this green leaf to announce to Noah the return of life on the earth in the form of some small plants, and therefore the olive signifies peace on earth until now.

8.7.0.en: Noah waited another seven days for the water to dry completely from the earth, and sent out the dove again and kept waiting for it until the end of the day, and it did not return to him, so he knew that the water had almost dried up in most places of the earth.

8.7.1.en: This search took about two months, during which anxiety covered Noah and his heart longed to know how dry the earth was, and he continued searching, but in the end he could not come out until God commanded him to. Would that he had kept silent and let God teach him at the proper time, but this is human weakness, which wants to know the facts by itself and cannot except with God's help.

8.7.2.en: Rely on God, confident of His ordering of your life, for He who has kept you throughout your past life is able to order your life in the future, so ask Him for your needs, and if their fulfillment is delayed, do not be troubled, for He is always with you as long as you want Him.

8.8.0.en: The covering: the roof of the ark, which was made of wood or animal skins.

8.8.1.en: Noah's anxiety and search about the dryness of the earth continued, so he removed the covering of the ark to see the sky clearly and look upon the earth. This was in the six hundred and first year of his age, on the first day of the first month of it, and he found that the earth had dried in most places, and he went on observing the earth over the days until the twenty-seventh day of the second month of the six hundred and first year of his age, when he noticed that the earth was completely dry. Thus this search of his took about two months, as we mentioned.

8.9.0.en: The first thing Noah did after coming out of the ark was to build an altar and offer sacrifices of the clean animals and birds, and it is implicitly understood that he learned this from Adam and his forefathers. Thus Noah's feelings toward God appear in his thanking Him for saving him, his family and all the humanity that would come after him from destruction, with all the animals, and in his obedience in offering the sacrifices that God had commanded for being pleased with man, which are a type of the sacrifice of Christ on the Cross, by which He gives us new life in Him.

8.9.1.en: God your heavenly Father gives you much and cares for you all day, so the least you can do is to thank Him for His gifts, and you rejoice His heart, and your heart too is filled with joy from your feeling of God who is with you, keeps you and blesses you.

8.10.0.en: God rejoiced in Noah's sacrifices and was pleased with him, or with mankind in his person, and promised not to destroy all men again with a total destruction, finding an excuse for man in that he is liable to fall into evil from his youth, that is, since the expulsion of Adam from the garden. And if He destroyed the whole world once by a flood, it was to declare to mankind His hatred of evil so that they might live in goodness, but in His tenderness He is long-suffering toward them and will no longer destroy them by a flood or anything else with a total destruction, and He will not curse the earth, but it will be blessed, it and all creatures, for the sake of man who loves God and worships Him.

8.11.0.en: God declares the existence of natural changes through the year, which He permits in order to alert man to repent and return to Him. For every year there is a time for sowing and also a time for harvesting the crops, and there are also the seasons of the year in which the temperature of the air differs: in winter and its extension, spring, the air tends to be cold, while in summer and its extension, autumn, the air tends to be hot. These seasons suit man psychologically and physically, but he should not be alarmed by them, for they will not turn into a total destruction for him, and so God declares His love for man, that perhaps He may draw him to Himself. Thus the fear of God that man sees in the Flood mixes with His love that he sees in His promise not to destroy man again, and the two help man to leave sin and live with God.

9.0.0.en: God gave a blessing to Noah and his sons that they might multiply and bear sons and daughters with whom to fill the earth, as He blessed Adam of old with the same blessing (ch. 1:28), because Noah is the beginning of the new humanity after the Flood.

9.0.1.en: May you have spiritual fruits and virtues, and may you grow in the love of God and fill the earth around you with works of goodness, lifting up prayers and praises, so that every day you fulfill the purpose of your creation and truly become the head of creation and the light of the world.

9.1.0.en: Since man pleased God, He gave him authority over all the animals, for although many of them are bigger and stronger than man, he rules over them by his wisdom and God's guidance to him, and thus God confirms that man is the head of creation. Man's food until this time was the plants and the fruits of the trees, but God now permitted him to eat meat, animals and birds, whether those on the earth or in the sea and everything that flies in the heaven; that is, man was a vegetarian until the Flood, and therefore his life was long.

9.2.0.en: God warned mankind against drinking blood or eating flesh with its blood, and Christianity confirmed this at the Council of Jerusalem in the year 50 AD (Acts 15:29), for the following reasons:

9.2.2.en: 2- Blood represents the life of animal and man, and God alone is the Giver of life, so not drinking blood is respect for the mystery of life and for God who gives it.

9.3.0.en: God also warns man against presuming, after slaughtering an animal, to slaughter or kill a man. He declares the importance of man's life in His sight and that He will punish the killer, whether an animal, as is stated in the Law of Moses (Ex 21:28-31), or a man, either by God's punishing him directly or by means of the civil laws that punish the killer, because man is the image of God, so his life is precious.

9.4.0.en: He confirms the same meaning of God's blessing mentioned in (v. 1).

9.5.0.en: God's fatherhood appears in His concern for man, who may live in fear of total destruction as happened in the Flood. So in order to give him reassurance, He made a covenant with him in the person of Noah, but it was given to his sons and all the humanity that would come from him and to all the animals that serve him. This covenant is a gift of love from one side, which is God, not tied to man's faithfulness and response to God, to show the love of God, His tenderness and His long-suffering, which remind man of the hideousness of sin and its punishment, that is, destruction, and how God holds it back from man to give him an opportunity to repent.

9.6.0.en: The covenant is not to destroy mankind by a flood again.

9.7.0.en: The sign of the covenant appears when the rains fall, so that man would not fear their increasing to the point of the world's destruction, God gives a sign in the heaven that appears in the clouds, which is what is known as the rainbow, that is, the refraction of the sun's rays on the water particles in the clouds, so the seven colors of the spectrum appear. And this covenant is still fulfilled until now whenever the rains fall heavily.

9.7.1.en: And as God's wrath was expressed through nature in the Flood, He also gave the sign of His love and care through nature in the rainbow.

9.7.2.en: The sign is a bow, for as man defends himself by using the bow and arrows, God defends His children and protects them from the punishment of their sins by the sign of the rainbow, to alert them to His love and call them to repentance so that they may obtain their salvation.

9.7.3.en: In the Book of Revelation God shows His love by the appearance of a rainbow around His heavenly throne, a sign of His love and care for His children (Rev 4:3, 10:1). In the New Testament God shows His love in bearing our sins on the Cross, then gives us the sign of His love perceptibly in the sacraments of the Church.

9.7.4.en: And when He says "I will remember my covenant", it does not mean that God had forgotten, but He expresses Himself in the way that men understand, and means to alert them to His constant mercies and His concern for them, so as to reassure them and keep them away from evil.

9.7.5.en: Contemplate God's mercies upon you in your past life, and if you can, write them down for yourself so that your heart may be at rest, and do not worry about the circumstances around you but thank Him and strive to cling to Him and give up your base desires. We note that Noah is a type of Christ in the following:

9.7.6.en: 1- Noah found grace in the eyes of God because of his righteousness, and the Father called to Christ from heaven, "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased" (Mt 3:17).

9.7.7.en: 2- Noah obeyed God and built the ark by which He saved those who believed in God, and Christ obeyed the Father and acquired His Church, by which He saves all who believe in Him.

9.7.8.en: 3- The world rejected Noah's message of repentance and entering the ark, and the Jewish nation of Christ rejected His message and mocked Him and even crucified Him.

9.7.9.en: 4- Noah and those with him were saved in the ark that floats on the waters and came out to a new life, and Christ saves those who believe in Him in the water of Baptism and begets them with a new birth.

9.7.10.en: 5- Noah offered a sacrifice of thanksgiving to God after coming out of the ark, and Christ offers His Body and Blood as a sacrifice of thanksgiving (Eucharist) on the altar every day.

9.7.11.en: 6- God promised Noah not to destroy the world by a flood again and gave him a sign, which is the rainbow, and God promises all who believe in His Son salvation and the Kingdom and has given them the sign, which is the Cross.

9.8.0.en: He mentions Noah's sons, who began to beget in the earth, and mentions the name of the son of one of them, Canaan the son of Ham, because of his part in the following event when Noah became drunk.

9.9.0.en: It appears that Noah, after coming out of the ark, was occupied with building dwellings for himself and his sons, and when the affairs of living were settled he began to work in farming, so he planted a vineyard.

9.10.0.en: Life became comfortable, so he sat drinking the fermented juice of the grapes inside his tent and was absorbed in the pleasure of drinking, so he drank much until he became drunk and lost consciousness and was uncovered, stripped of all his clothes. This conduct was extremely strange, because it concerns a saint who kept himself pure for 600 years despite the many wicked people around him who were absorbed in their desires, among them drunkenness, which leads to nakedness and to falling into various sins. But it appears that after he received the divine covenant and was at rest in all the matters of his life, he gave up his exactness and his vigilance against sin, so he allowed himself to be absorbed in pleasure until he became drunk, and the effects of the sin of drunkenness appeared, which is the shame that came upon him when he was uncovered.

9.10.1.en: Be exact throughout your life and do not be lax with evil, and when God keeps you from the wars of the demons, seize it as an opportunity for spiritual growth, and do not be lax with sin however small, lest you be stripped of the garments of your righteousness.

9.11.0.en: Ham, the son of Noah, passed by his father's tent and noticed his drunkenness and nakedness, and he did not cover him and shield him, but on the contrary mocked him and went to expose him before his brothers Shem and Japheth. It appears that Canaan shared with him in seeing Noah naked and in mocking him, and Canaan may have been the first to see his grandfather uncovered and told his father Ham, who came and saw him and shared in mocking and exposing him, and therefore the curse came afterward upon Canaan.

9.12.0.en: The conduct of Shem and Japheth was entirely balanced, for they did not lose their respect for their father because of his sin, but thought positively how to cover him. So they took a garment, probably in the form of a cloak, and went to the tent, and before they came near it they turned their backs to the door of the tent, put the garment on their backs and walked toward the door, and covered their father without seeing him in his nakedness, and they did not share in mocking their father, and they may even have rebuked Ham and Canaan for what they had done.

9.13.0.en: When Noah awoke from his wine and saw himself covered with the garment, he asked his sons and learned what they had done, and was vexed at the conduct of Canaan his grandson toward him. In the spirit of prophecy he punished Canaan, saying that he would be a servant to his brothers, that is, that his descendants would be enslaved to the descendants of his brothers, and he did not curse his father Ham because God had blessed him with his brothers (v. 1). This actually happened with the domination of the descendants of Shem and Japheth over the Canaanites, for the people of God under the leadership of Joshua entered the land of Canaan and dominated them. As for the descendants of Shem and Japheth, he prophesied blessing for them, and this actually happened, for the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob came from the descendants of Shem, and likewise the people of God and Moses and then Christ. He also blessed the descendants of Japheth, who are those who dwelt in the continent of Europe. The curse was upon Canaan only, the son of Ham, and not upon all the sons of Ham, such as Cush and Mizraim, who dwelt in Africa. And the descendants of Japheth, that is, the Europeans, dwelt in the East, Africa, the Americas and Australia, as Noah prophesied for them.

9.14.0.en: Noah lived long and completed 950 years, so he is the third man in length of life after Methuselah and Jared, but after that man's life became shorter.

9.14.1.en: The life of Noah can be summarized as follows:

9.14.2.en: 1- Noah finds grace in the eyes of God among the wicked. (ch. 6)

9.14.3.en: 2- God's command to him to build the ark. (ch. 6)

9.14.4.en: 3- Building the ark and bringing in the animals and then his family. (ch. 6, 7)

9.14.6.en: 5- The abating of the waters and the resting of the ark on Mount Ararat (ch. 8)

9.14.7.en: 6- His sending out the raven and the dove and then his coming out of the ark. (ch. 8)

9.14.8.en: 7- Building an altar and offering a sacrifice of thanksgiving. (ch. 8)

9.14.9.en: 8- God's promise not to destroy the world again by a flood and His giving him the sign of the rainbow. (ch. 9)

9.14.10.en: 9- His drunkenness and nakedness, his two sons' covering him, and his cursing of Canaan. (ch. 9)

9.14.11.en: 10- The death of Noah and his descendants. (ch. 9, 10) The descendants of Noah
